scope: compute queue inspect/candidates only; not a whole-application benchmark

dataset.description: Synthetic storage/performance fixtures, not actually executed Runs or development workloads.

lockWait.method: Separate Node process/SQLite connection held BEGIN IMMEDIATE for a nominal 200 ms; the benchmark connection measured acquiring its own write transaction.

plans.sql: SELECT * FROM compute_queue WHERE phase NOT IN ('succeeded','failed','cancelled','timed_out') AND sequence>?  ORDER BY sequence LIMIT ?
details: SEARCH compute_queue USING INTEGER PRIMARY KEY (rowid>?)

plans.sql: SELECT target_id FROM compute_contexts WHERE target_id IS NOT NULL UNION SELECT target_id FROM compute_queue WHERE held=1 AND target_id IS NOT NULL UNION SELECT target_id FROM compute_queue WHERE phase='queued' AND target_id IS NOT NULL UNION SELECT 'host-example' target_id ORDER BY target_id LIMIT 256
details: USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY
SEARCH compute_queue USING COVERING INDEX compute_queue_occupancy (held=? AND target_id>?)

plans.sql:
WITH eligible AS (
SELECT q.* FROM compute_queue q JOIN compute_limits h ON h.target_id='host' LEFT JOIN compute_limits t ON t.target_id=q.target_id
WHERE q.phase='queued' AND q.bound=1 AND q.next_attempt_at<=? AND (q.backend='trusted-example' OR EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM compute_contexts c WHERE c.context=q.context_name AND c.status='ready' AND c.engine_id=q.engine_id AND c.endpoint=q.endpoint AND c.next_probe_at>?))
AND ((CASE WHEN json_type(t.data,'$.cpus') IS NULL THEN json_extract(h.data,'$.cpus') ELSE json_extract(t.data,'$.cpus') END) IS NULL OR q.cpu_millis<=(CASE WHEN json_type(t.data,'$.cpus') IS NULL THEN json_extract(h.data,'$.cpus') ELSE json_extract(t.data,'$.cpus') END)*1000) AND (json_extract(h.data,'$.cpus') IS NULL OR q.cpu_millis<=json_extract(h.data,'$.cpus')*1000) AND ((CASE WHEN json_type(t.data,'$.memoryMb') IS NULL THEN json_extract(h.data,'$.memoryMb') ELSE json_extract(t.data,'$.memoryMb') END) IS NULL OR q.memory_mb<=(CASE WHEN json_type(t.data,'$.memoryMb') IS NULL THEN json_extract(h.data,'$.memoryMb') ELSE json_extract(t.data,'$.memoryMb') END)*1) AND (json_extract(h.data,'$.memoryMb') IS NULL OR q.memory_mb<=json_extract(h.data,'$.memoryMb')*1)
AND (CASE WHEN json_type(t.data,'$.maxJobs') IS NULL THEN json_extract(h.data,'$.maxJobs') ELSE json_extract(t.data,'$.maxJobs') END)>=1 AND json_extract(h.data,'$.maxJobs')>=1
AND (q.kind='run' AND (CASE WHEN json_type(t.data,'$.maxRuns') IS NULL THEN json_extract(h.data,'$.maxRuns') ELSE json_extract(t.data,'$.maxRuns') END)>=1 AND json_extract(h.data,'$.maxRuns')>=1 OR q.kind='development' AND (CASE WHEN json_type(t.data,'$.maxDevelopment') IS NULL THEN json_extract(h.data,'$.maxDevelopment') ELSE json_extract(t.data,'$.maxDevelopment') END)>=1 AND json_extract(h.data,'$.maxDevelopment')>=1)),
heads AS (SELECT target_id,min(sequence) sequence FROM eligible GROUP BY target_id)
SELECT e.* FROM eligible e JOIN heads h ON h.sequence=e.sequence ORDER BY e.sequence LIMIT 256
details: SEARCH t USING INDEX sqlite_autoindex_compute_limits_1 (target_id=?) LEFT-JOIN
USE TEMP B-TREE FOR GROUP BY

SELECT count(*) jobs,COALESCE(sum(kind='run'),0) runs,COALESCE(sum(kind='development'),0) development,COALESCE(sum(cpu_millis),0) cpu,COALESCE(sum(memory_mb),0) memory,COALESCE(sum(phase='unknown'),0) unknown FROM compute_queue WHERE held=1
SELECT version,data FROM compute_limits WHERE target_id=?

SELECT count(*) jobs,COALESCE(sum(kind='run'),0) runs,COALESCE(sum(kind='development'),0) development,COALESCE(sum(cpu_millis),0) cpu,COALESCE(sum(memory_mb),0) memory,COALESCE(sum(phase='unknown'),0) unknown FROM compute_queue WHERE held=1 AND (target_id=? OR (?<>'host-example' AND backend='docker' AND bound=0))
SELECT count(*) n FROM compute_queue WHERE phase='queued'
details: SEARCH compute_queue USING COVERING INDEX compute_queue_phase_sequence (phase=?)

limitations: Measurements cover ComputeQueue.inspect and ComputeQueue.candidates only, under the recorded synthetic dataset.
They do not establish whole-application speedups, eliminate every other full scan, or measure Docker workload throughput.
EXPLAIN retains context-table scans, temporary B-trees and the derived-head scan; this is not a claim that all SQL operations are index-only.
No claim is made about production load isolation, GPU, remote targets or model HTTP concurrency.
